_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mauritania covering Berber-Arab nomadic heritage, Ghana Empire overlap, trans-Saharan trade, Almoravid movement, French colonisation, slavery abolition (last country 1981/2007 criminalisation), military coups, and Sahel security.

ethnic_groups.name: Moors/Maure (Bidhan - White Moors)
ethnic_groups.notes: Arab-Berber; Hassaniya Arabic-speaking; historically dominant politically and economically; nomadic heritage; include various tribes/qabila

ethnic_groups.name: Haratine (Black Moors/Haratin)
ethnic_groups.notes: Arabized Black Africans; Hassaniya-speaking; historically enslaved or descended from enslaved; largest single group but politically marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Fula/Fulani (Halpulaar)
ethnic_groups.notes: West African; Pulaar-speaking; Senegal River valley; pastoralists and farmers; part of 'Black African' or Afro-Mauritanian bloc

ethnic_groups.name: Soninke (Sarakolé)
ethnic_groups.notes: Mande people; Senegal River valley; Ghana Empire heritage; merchant tradition

ethnic_groups.name: Wolof
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Mauritania; fishermen and traders; cross-border with Senegal

country_profile.notes_slavery: Last country to abolish slavery (1981); criminalized 2007; legacy remains contentious with Haratine community activism
country_profile.notes_unique: Bridges Arab North Africa and sub-Saharan West Africa; the Richat Structure ('Eye of the Sahara') is a 40 km geological formation visible from space; last country to legally abolish slavery (1981).

natural_resources.notes: SNIM iron ore (Zouérat mine/Nouadhibou railway, one of world's longest trains); Tasiast gold mine (Kinross); fishing waters among richest in the world; gas discovery (GTA field with BP/Kosmos); artisanal gold mining booming.

military.notes: President Ghazouani is former army chief; military historically central to politics (multiple coups); counterterrorism operations in Sahel (AQIM); successful in reducing jihadist attacks post-2011.

infrastructure.notes: Limited infrastructure; iron ore railway; Mattel, Mauritel telecoms; Nouakchott sprawling.

debt_aid.notes: Heavily indebted (HIPC); gas revenues expected to transform economy (GTA field first gas expected 2024-25); slavery legacy creates socioeconomic stratification; Gulf states provide aid.

education.notes: Bilingual education system (Arabic/French) contentious politically; mahadra (traditional Koranic school) tradition; low female secondary enrollment in rural areas; slavery legacy affects education access for Haratine community.

diaspora_migration.notes: Hosts Malian refugees in Mbera camp; 1989 Senegal-Mauritania crisis expelled thousands of Black Mauritanians; Haratine (descendants of slaves) remain marginalised.

digital_economy.notes: ACE submarine cable; mobile penetration over 100%; Mauritel (Maroc Telecom) and Mattel primary operators; data costs relatively high; Nouakchott concentrates most tech activity.

country_profile.national_anthem: Bilāda l-ʾUbāti l-Hudāti l-Kirām (Land of the Proud, Guided Ones)

geography.terrain: Sahara desert dominates; Sahel in south; Senegal River valley; Adrar Plateau; barren plains (reg/erg)
geography.notes: Bridge between Arab Maghreb and Sub-Saharan Africa; Richat Structure ('Eye of Africa/Sahara'); Banc d'Arguin (UNESCO, migratory birds); iron ore railway (world's longest train).

economy_extended.notes: Iron ore (SNIM, 2nd largest African producer); gold mining; fisheries (octopus, EU agreements); offshore gas (GTA/Grand Tortue Ahmeyim field with Senegal); livestock.

health.notes: High maternal mortality; urban-rural healthcare disparity; traditional medicine; Nouakchott hospitals serve entire country.

food_agriculture.notes: Predominantly pastoral economy; Senegal River valley rice/agriculture; dates in oases; high food import dependency; livestock transhumance.

energy.notes: GTA gas field (with BP/Senegal) expected 2024+; Manantali hydro shared; solar/wind expansion; SOMELEC utility.

transport.notes: World's longest freight train (SNIM iron ore, up to 2.5 km); Route de l'Espoir (Nouakchott–Néma); poor road network outside main highways.

unesco_sites_list: Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt, and Oualata
major_attractions: Chinguetti (7th holy city of Islam, manuscripts)
tourism.notes: Desert tourism niche; Chinguetti manuscripts/libraries; Richat Structure geological wonder; very small tourism sector.

human_rights_gender.notes: Modern slavery/descent-based slavery persists (Haratine); abolished slavery 1981 (last in world); criminalized 2007; anti-slavery activists imprisoned; FGM widespread; blasphemy laws.

security_stability.notes: Successfully contained jihadist threat (G5 Sahel member); relatively stable despite Sahel neighbors' crises; 2019 peaceful transfer of power.

cultural_heritage.national_dish: Thieboudienne (rice and fish, shared with Senegal)
cultural_heritage.film_industry: Minimal (Timbuktu by Abderrahmane Sissako, nominated Oscar 2015)
notable_historical_figures: Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz (2008 coup leader)
world_heritage_sites: Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt, and Oualata
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: TVM state; limited private media; government controls; Al Akhbar (online); social media growing
cultural_heritage.notes: Arab-African bridge; Moorish culture; tea ceremony (atay) central to social life; Chinguetti manuscripts; descent-based slavery legacy.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Islamic law (Sharia) and French civil law blend
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Applicable in personal status and criminal law
legal_system.notes: Islamic republic; Sharia primary source of law; apostasy punishable by death (not enforced in practice); Supreme Court.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.

current_leader.name: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former general; Aziz's ally and successor; UPR party; first peaceful democratic transition between elected leaders; re-elected 2024

former_leaders.name: Moktar Ould Daddah
former_leaders.notes: Founding president; Arab nationalist; Western Sahara annexation attempt; overthrown by military

former_leaders.name: Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler; 21 years; recognized Israel 1999; overthrown in 2005 coup while abroad

former_leaders.name: Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi
former_leaders.notes: First democratically elected; overthrown by Aziz after 16 months

former_leaders.name: Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz
former_leaders.notes: General who led 2008 coup; elected 2009 and 2014; stepped down constitutionally 2019; corruption trial 2023

910.name: Prehistoric Saharan Mauritania
910.description: Neolithic pastoral communities in the 'Green Sahara'; rock art; gradual desiccation pushes populations southward.

sub_clusters.name: Green Sahara and Pastoral Communities
sub_clusters.description: Pluvial period supports cattle pastoralism and fishing; Tichitt-Walata settlements among earliest in West Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Tichitt-Walata Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Stone-built settlements; millet cultivation; possible proto-Soninke urbanisation; precursor to Ghana Empire.

920.name: Sanhaja Berber Confederation and Ghana Empire Overlap
920.description: Sanhaja Berber nomads dominate the western Sahara; overlap with Ghana Empire territory; trans-Saharan caravan routes.

sub_clusters.name: Sanhaja Berber Nomadic Confederations
sub_clusters.description: Lamtuna, Gudala, and Massufa Sanhaja control Saharan trade routes; Audaghost as key entrepôt.

sub_clusters.name: Ghana Empire in Southern Mauritania
sub_clusters.description: Koumbi Saleh (in modern Mauritania) serves as Ghana's capital; gold-salt trade axis.

920.name: Almoravid Movement
920.description: Abdallah ibn Yasin launches Almoravid jihad from Mauritanian ribat; movement conquers Morocco and Al-Andalus.

sub_clusters.name: Ibn Yasin's Ribat and Almoravid Origins
sub_clusters.description: Abdallah ibn Yasin establishes ribat (possibly on Tidra island); strict Maliki reform movement among Sanhaja.

sub_clusters.name: Almoravid Conquests from Mauritania
sub_clusters.description: Almoravids conquer Audaghost, Ghana, Morocco, and cross into Iberia; Mauritania as movement's cradle.

930.name: Arab Migration and Beni Hassan Dominance
930.description: Beni Hassan Arab warriors migrate into Mauritania; Char Bouba War; Arabic supplants Berber; Hassaniya culture forms.

sub_clusters.name: Beni Hassan Arab Migration
sub_clusters.description: Maqil Arab groups migrate southward; establish warrior aristocracy over Berber (Znaga) populations.

sub_clusters.name: Char Bouba War (Thirty-Year War)
sub_clusters.description: Decisive war between Berber Zawaya clerics and Arab Hassan warriors; Hassan triumph establishes social hierarchy.

sub_clusters.name: Trans-Saharan Trade Routes
sub_clusters.description: Salt from Idjil mines; gold, slaves, and gum arabic traded; Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt, and Oualata as caravan towns.

940.name: French Colonisation of Mauritania
940.description: French establish control from Senegal; Xavier Coppolani's pacification; colonial territory within AOF with minimal development.

sub_clusters.name: Coppolani's Pacification Campaign
sub_clusters.description: Xavier Coppolani uses diplomacy with Zawaya clerics to establish French authority; assassinated 1905.

sub_clusters.name: Mauritania within AOF
sub_clusters.description: Minimal colonial investment; capital in Saint-Louis (Senegal); nomadic resistance continues until 1930s.

sub_clusters.name: Gum Arabic Trade under Colonialism
sub_clusters.description: Gum arabic trade on the Senegal River drives French commercial interest; escale (trading post) system.

950.name: Independence and Mokhtar Ould Daddah Era
950.description: Independence 1960; Daddah's one-party state; Arabisation policies; disastrous Western Sahara War leads to his overthrow.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Mauritania
sub_clusters.description: Mauritania independent 28 November 1960; Mokhtar Ould Daddah president; Morocco contests sovereignty.

sub_clusters.name: Arabisation and Racial Tensions
sub_clusters.description: Arabic imposed as official language; Haratin and Black African communities marginalised; 1966 ethnic riots.

sub_clusters.name: Western Sahara War
sub_clusters.description: Mauritania and Morocco partition Western Sahara; Polisario Front attacks; war bankrupts Mauritania; Daddah ousted.

950.name: Military Rule and Coups
950.description: Series of military coups; Ould Taya's long rule (1984–2005); slavery persists; democratic façade.

sub_clusters.name: Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya Era
sub_clusters.description: Taya seizes power 1984; cautious liberalisation; 1989 Senegal-Mauritania crisis; recognises Israel 1999; overthrown 2005.

sub_clusters.name: Slavery Abolition and Persistence
sub_clusters.description: Slavery abolished 1905 (French), 1981 (Mauritanian law—last country globally), criminalised 2007; persists in practice.

960.name: Contemporary Mauritania
960.description: Democratic transition attempts; Abdel Aziz coup and rule; Ghazouani presidency; Sahel security; mining economy.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Transition and 2008 Coup
sub_clusters.description: Ely Ould Mohamed Vall leads transition; Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi elected 2007; Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz coups 2008.

sub_clusters.name: Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Abdel Aziz elected 2009 and 2014; anti-terrorism operations; iron ore and oil revenues; later arrested for corruption.

sub_clusters.name: Ghazouani Presidency and Sahel Diplomacy
sub_clusters.description: Mohamed Ould Ghazouani elected in peaceful transfer; G5 Sahel counter-terrorism; cautious democratisation.

sub_clusters.name: Sahel Security and Counter-Terrorism
sub_clusters.description: AQIM attacks (2000s); successful counter-terrorism strategy; G5 Sahel partnership; relative stability compared to neighbours.
